source_receipts.captured_excerpt_text:
Coinbase Global, Inc. Form 10-Q for quarter ended September 30, 2026, filed October 29, 2026.
For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, net revenue was $1.2 billion and $3.7 billion, including $590.2 million and $1.9 billion in transaction revenue and $570.2 million and $1.7 billion in subscription and services revenue.
Stablecoin revenue: Q3 2026 $306.905 million; Q3 2025 $324.534 million; nine months 2026 $904.487 million; nine months 2025 $907.485 million.
During the first quarter of 2026, Coinbase revised the presentation of revenue earned on corporate payment stablecoin balances, presenting those amounts in Corporate interest and other income rather than Stablecoin revenue; prior-period amounts were reclassified.
Assets on Platform were $376.6 billion at September 30, 2026, versus $515.9 billion a year earlier.
The AOP asset table reports USDC at $8.616 billion on September 30, 2026, versus $9.013 billion a year earlier.
Coinbase said average USDC held in Coinbase products reached an all-time high during Q3; this average-period statement is not the same measure as quarter-end AOP USDC.
source_receipts.hash_scope: SHA-256 of normalized excerpt transcribed from the SEC filing lines cited in the research notes; not the entire filing HTML.
cited_filing_sections: MD&A executive overview and highlights, pp. 32–33
Subscription and services revenue table, p. 34
Assets on Platform by asset, p. 41
limitations: Issuer filing is primary evidence for company metrics, but quarter-end AOP USDC and average USDC held in products are different measurement scopes.
Q3 stablecoin revenue is not a disclosed XRP-specific revenue measure.

source_receipts.captured_excerpt_text:
Coinbase Form 10-Q, September 30, 2026.
Institutional financing loan receivables totaled $1.976137 billion; collateral requirements for outstanding loans ranged from 100% to 250% of loan fair value.
Recognized lending collateral totaled $1.009297 billion, including $920.649 million Bitcoin, $67.005 million Ethereum, $9.903 million other crypto assets, and $11.740 million fiat/payment stablecoins.
Customer collateral not recognized as collateral totaled $3.284562 billion, including $2.804112 billion crypto assets and $480.450 million fiat/payment stablecoins.
Other crypto assets are aggregated and none individually represented more than 5% of total crypto collateral; no XRP-specific collateral balance is disclosed.

source_receipts.publisher: Circle Internet Group, Inc. / U.S. SEC
source_receipts.captured_excerpt_text:
Circle Internet Group, Inc. Form 10-Q for quarter ended September 30, 2026, filed November 4, 2026.
Average USDC in circulation was $73.264 billion in Q3 2026 versus $67.842 billion in Q3 2025; end-of-period USDC circulation was $73.879 billion.
USDC onchain transaction volume grew 49% to $13.9 trillion.
Q3 reserve income was $657.624 million; other revenue was $207.264 million; total revenue and reserve income was $864.888 million.
Q3 reserve return rate was 3.5%; USDC on platform at period end was $13.868 billion, a Circle-defined measure including Circle Mint, corporate-held USDC and certain Circle wallet balances.
Under the Collaboration Agreement with Coinbase, Coinbase receives allocations based on USDC held on its platform after issuer retention and half of remaining amount tied to broader ecosystem growth after approved third-party ecosystem participants.
Circle incurred $331.3 million Q3 2026 distribution costs in connection with its agreements with Coinbase and $986.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
Circle launched Arc public mainnet in September 2026. Arc is a separate Circle Layer-1 network, not XRPL.
Circle's Q3 filing reports 807.5 million ARC tokens sold under institutional purchase agreements at $0.30 per token for approximately $242.2 million aggregate gross proceeds; initial ARC supply is 10 billion.
source_receipts.hash_scope: SHA-256 of normalized excerpt transcribed from SEC filing, including Q3 operating indicators, Coinbase collaboration terms, distribution-cost disclosure and Arc/ARC sections; not entire filing HTML.
limitations: Circle's distribution-cost measure and Coinbase's stablecoin-revenue measure are different accounting line items and must not be netted or interpreted as a direct profit split.
Circle's USDC-on-platform measure is not Coinbase AOP USDC.
Arc is not XRPL and ARC is not XRP.
